entities.summary:
Ottobuono di Razzi was an Italian clergyman and feudal lord who served as Patriarch of Aquileia from 1302 until his death in 1315. A key figure in the Catholic Church during the Late Middle Ages, Ottobuono played a significant role in the governance of the Church in Italy.

Born in the 13th century, Ottobuono rose through the ranks of the Church to become Patriarch of Aquileia, a position that gave him significant authority over the Church's affairs in the region. His tenure was marked by several notable events, including the Papal Schism of 1309-1314, which pitted Ottobuono against the Pope, Clement V.

Despite the challenges posed by the schism, Ottobuono continued to assert his authority and secure the support of the powerful nobility in the region. His leadership and diplomacy helped to maintain stability in the Church and secured the interests of the Catholic Church in Italy.

Ottobuono's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a crucial role in shaping the Church's response to the Black Death, which devastated Europe in the 14th century. His efforts helped to establish the Church as a primary provider of humanitarian aid and support during this time of crisis.

Today, Ottobuono di Razzi is remembered as a significant figure in the history of the Catholic Church, particularly in Italy. His commitment to the Church's teachings and his leadership during a time of great challenge have made him an important figure in the annals of Church history.
